stories.title: US flights resume after rare hours-long nationwide grounding but cancellations, delays persist
summary: Weary travellers braced for more delays and cancellations on Saturday as flights resumed from US airports after being grounded for four hours due to a major outage on outdated communications systems.
Yeah, you know, it’s just a mess, right?” Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP, as she waited for a flight Saturday morning at New York’s La Guardia airport.

So they’re flying today and for that I’m grateful.” Decades-old equipment The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos; it has raised serious concerns about the country’s ageing infrastructure.

stories.title: Microsoft announces service 'restored,' global outage over
summary: Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents”.
It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant.
Microsoft on Friday apologised for the global outage as it reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services.

stories.title: Mir Raza murder case: Ex-SHO dismissed over misconduct, mishandling of evidence
summary: Last month, a joint investigation team (JIT) constituted by the Sindh government recommended an inquiry against Qureshi, who was suspended from duty, over the possible facilitation of the destruction of evidence.

The order further noted that an inquiry was conducted by Central Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Muhammad Imran Khan, who observed that Qureshi not only failed to discharge his duties in securing the crime scene and evidence, but did not even visit the site.

In its 62-page report, the commission, while severely criticising the police investigation, came to the conclusion that it was a “murder”, and made a host of recommendations, including formation of a joint investigation team (JIT) to probe the case.

stories.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16
summary: The 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers will be held in Islamabad on Nov 15 and 16, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

The meeting will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies, the FO said in a statement.
During the summit, Pakistan called for enhanced intra-regional trade, transport connectivity, energy cooperation and sustainable development, while reaffirming its commitment to the ECO Vision 2025.

stories.title: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR
summary: Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday.

On the night of Nov 13/14 in Kolpur, security forces “successfully neutralised eight Indian-sponsored terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan (FAH), including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition”, ISPR said.
In an earlier statement, ISPR said two soldiers were martyred and 16 terrorists were killed as security forces continued a series of IBOs in North Waziristan.

stories.title: India stun Pakistan by one wicket in last-ball U-19 Asia Cup final thriller
summary: Mohit Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata held their nerve to guide India to a dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the ACC Men’s U-19 Asia Cup final, chasing down a target of 338 on the final ball at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Saturday.
With eight runs required in the final over, Ulva, who finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, including five fours and three sixes, struck the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain’s final delivery.
Qadir provided the acceleration with an attacking 80 off just 54 balls, hitting three fours and eight sixes before being dismissed on the last ball of the 27th over with Pakistan at 197 for two.

stories.title: NCCIA warns youth against joining illegal call centres for lucrative salaries
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Saturday warned that loopholes in the existing system are being exploited by illegal call centres, online betting operators and international fraud networks to launder money and trap victims.

The operators then take that company’s bank account and integrate it with their online betting or gaming portal,” Khan said, adding that the NCCIA team is working on recommendations to these institutions so that they improve their checking systems.
The NCCIA additional director noted the agency raided two call centres in the Islamabad-Rawalpindi Zone over the past three days.

stories.title: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz discuss country's political, economic and security situation
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday discussed the country’s political, economic and security situation in detail, the premier’s office said.
President Zardari’s meeting with the premier comes just two days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called on the president.

The last publicly reported meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz was on Oct 10, where the two discussed the country’s security situation just a day before the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: FO says Climate Minister Musadik Malik nominated to represent Pakistan at SCO moot in New Delhi
summary: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday that Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik had been nominated to represent Pakistan at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi from Nov 20-22.

In a press briefing on Friday, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India has invited several SCO member states to take part in the dialogue, adding that New Delhi looks forward to hosting the gathering.

Pakistan’s chairmanship of SCO CHS marks another step in the country’s growing engagement with the regional organisation, which has expanded its focus from security cooperation to economic development and regional connectivity.

stories.title: Pakistan, 16 other countries, condemn Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital
summary: Pakistan and 16 other countries,on Saturday condemned the Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, calling on Tel Aviv to protect civilians and medical facilities and ensure the sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid to the Palestinian enclave.

Earlier this month, the Trump’s “Board of Peace” said that Israel needed to act immediately to help war-battered Gaza cope with impending winter, saying measures ahead of deadly floods had been insufficient.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Nov 9 said he had directed the foreign ministry to pursue all possible means to urgently “escalate humanitarian assistance” to Gaza amid heavy rainfall.

stories.title: Achakzai, Abbas move FCC for release of Sohail Afridi, detained lawmakers
summary: The petition also sought disclosure of the places of detention, production of the alleged detainees before the FCC, a declaration that their custody was unlawful and without lawful authority, and appropriate constitutional relief in the interest of justice and the rule of law.
However, the FCC on Nov 5 restrained the high court from hearing cases concerning the arrests of scores of PTI activists detained under the ordinance.
The application said the FCC’s Nov 5 order directly affected their constitutional rights.

stories.title: Pakistan’s polio paradox
summary: Pakistan has not turned its abi­­lity to run campaigns into a system of public health protection that families trust, and that failure, which lies behind much of the refusal, is why the virus survives.

For families who see little improvement in their lives, each arrival of a polio team can confirm that the state cares about one disease and one campaign, and little about the wellbeing of their children.

That takes trained health workers, reliable vaccine supplies, accessible facilities, and continuity of care, well beyond the occasional catch-up activities atta­ched to polio campaigns, so that immunisation beco­mes a regular function of the district health system.

stories.title: Mineral wealth
summary: PAKISTAN’S mineral wealth offers an opportunity to attract investment, earn foreign exchange and support long-term economic growth.
At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026, Deputy PM Ishaq Dar has promised predictable policies and institutional support to investors interested in the country’s mineral resources.
But no country has ever developed on mineral wealth or exports alone.

stories.title: KP Governor Kundi announces suspension of gold mining across province
summary: Addressing a press conference in Peshawar, Governor Kundi condemned the attack in Kohat that claimed the lives of 10 police personnel returning from an operation against illegal mining in the region.
On the Kohat incident, Governor Kundi said that following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule, the administration had launched an operation against illegal gold mining.

The governor assured that there would be no political victimisation, adding that anyone found involved in the nexus would be held accountable. “If there is no system of reward and punishment, neither this province nor this country will move forward.

stories.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman, sources say
summary: His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive ⁠of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, whom the US was investigating for potentially spying for China.
In two separate messages in October, ‌Huang told ⁠Nvidia leaders, including Teter and Wagonfeld, that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers.

Nvidia's Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.

stories.title: Pakistan, Uzbekistan reaffirm commitment to expanding defence cooperation during air chief's visit
summary: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu on Saturday held meetings with Uzbekistan's defence leadership on an official visit to the country, with discussions focusing on strengthening bilateral defence cooperation, joint military exercises and institutional collaboration.

In a statement posted on X, the DGPR (Air Force) said that discussions with Uzbek Defence Minister Lieutenant General Botir Qudrathodjayev Bahromovich focused on "regional security, existing defence ties and prospects for institutional collaboration".
The statement further noted that Air Chief Sidhu highlighted the deep-rooted brotherly ties between Pakistan and Uzbekistan.

stories.title: ‘A moral red line’? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution
summary: Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy.
The United States refers to an “appropriate level of human judgement” in the use of autonomous weapons.

The autonomous weapons to be discussed in Geneva are not yet in widespread use, although analysts have noted that they have been deployed by Russia in its invasion of Ukraine as well as US attacks in Iran.

stories.title: Army officer and soldier martyred, 8 terrorists killed in ongoing Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
summary: It said that on the night between Friday and Saturday, "security forces successfully neutralised eight Indian-sponsored terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan (FAH), including a suicide bomber and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition" in Kolpur.

The ISPR said that "India continues to give FAH full financial support and supply it with the latest gadgetry," noting, however, that security forces "are fully alive to this evolving threat and will deny the terrorists any space, whatever means they employ".

The martyrs will always remain alive in our hearts." Earlier in the day, the ISPR noted that two soldiers were martyred while 16 terrorists, including two Afghan nationals, were killed during IBOs in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's North Waziristan district over the past 12 hours.

stories.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
summary: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.
Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.
Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but will not be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

stories.title: Türkiye publishes law approving ratification of Makkah joint defence pact
summary: Turkish parliament approved the measure with 279 votes to 119 on November 5.
Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement during a trilateral summit in the holy city on Aug 7.
Saudi Arabia brings economic strength, regional influence and political leadership, while Turkiye contributes an advanced defence industry, military technology and industrial capacity.

stories.title: Pakistan, 16 other countries slam Israeli airstrike on Gaza hospital, warn against undermining ceasefire
summary: Pakistan and 16 other countries on Saturday condemned an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Gaza's Khan Younis that killed six people, including patients and healthcare workers, describing it as a violation of international humanitarian law.
Israel must implement them without further delay or additional conditions, including political and security conditions, that impede humanitarian access.
Urgent humanitarian assistance must proceed independently of progress on subsequent phases," the statement noted.

stories.title: President Zardari meets PM Shehbaz as debate over new provinces continues
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at his Model Town residence on Saturday, amid renewed political debate over the creation of new provinces.
New life in the debate followed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's proposal for a referendum on the issue, a proposal that has also found support among some Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PMLN) leaders.

Zardari's recent meeting with Naqvi in Nawabshah had also attracted attention in the context of the discussion on new provinces, although the President's House said the meeting had focused on national security and the regional situation.

stories.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
summary: SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and "chopstick"-arm technology to recover Starship's lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within minutes of ​the launch.
SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship's upper stage back to home base at the end of its ⁠flight.
SpaceX last launched Starship in September, taking the rocket and a payload of satellites to orbit for the first time despite some rocket engines malfunctioning in mid-flight.

stories.title: Police foil attack on checkpost in KP's Bannu, eliminate four terrorists
summary: BANNU: Police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu district on Friday night, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation, a police spokesperson said.

According to the police spokesperson, heavily armed terrorists launched a sudden attack on the checkpost last night. “However, police personnel deployed at the checkpost responded promptly and successfully repelled the assault,” he stated.

The spokesperson said that police also seized four Kalashnikov rifles, several magazines, a substantial quantity of ammunition, hand grenades and bandoliers, adding that the identification of the slain terrorists was underway.

stories.title: As smog hangs over Lahore, new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
summary: Read: Lahore tops global pollution rankings as AQI crosses 500 in several Punjab cities The unit ​is the first of its kind in Pakistan dedicated to fighting pollution, officials say, and it is one of ⁠the most visible steps in a campaign that Punjab officials claim is working.
Farmers caught burning stubble face fines of 15,000 Pakistani rupees ($54) ‌per ⁠acre, said Muhammad Farooq, an assistant director of the Punjab Agriculture Department.
Also read: Punjab blames India's Diwali fireworks for Lahore's toxic air India's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

stories.title: Wasim Akram questions Cummins’ Sandpapergate denial, says bowlers would spot tampering
summary: But the sandpaper scratch is totally different than the one-bounce scratch.” Wasim suggested that the difference could easily be identified through a simple comparison, saying anyone could take a semi-new ball, rub sandpaper against it and observe the resulting marks.
Khawaja alleged that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was widespread within the Australian dressing room, including among the bowling group, during the 2018 tour of South Africa.
The Australia captain maintained that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field and denied being an architect of the ball-tampering scheme.

stories.title: US to resume flights after air traffic network failure sparks chaos
summary: The United States Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centres caused chaos ​at US airports and triggered the longest shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks.

Earlier on Friday, before the outage, the White House and Department of Transportation had urged Congress to approve $30.1 billion to upgrade the nation's ageing airports and air traffic control infrastructure.
"What we ​have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," Duffy said.

stories.title: Pakistan needs 'middle-power alliances' to navigate emerging world order, US-China rivalry
summary: Pakistan would need to forge alliances and partnerships with "like-minded" middle powers to navigate the emerging world order and resist pressure to pick sides in the US-China rivalry.
Read: A world of blocs: where Pakistan stands The professor expounded: “Pakistan needs to form alliances with like-minded countries to be able to withstand pressure from great powers.

The professor added that unlike the Cold War, where countries fell neatly into one camp or another, in the current bipolar dispensation, most countries were “hedging their bets” and were looking for a “better offer” from either the US or China.

stories.title: Pakistan urges Gulf de-escalation as US, Iran trade accusations at UN
summary: Iranian missiles, drones and what she described as unlawful mines in the Strait of Hormuz, along with attacks in the Bab el-Mandab Strait, threatened global energy and food security.

Citing Security Council Resolution 2817, which demanded that Iran stop attacks on shipping and neighbouring states and had attracted 136 co-sponsors, she said Tehran was defying the international community. “Iran ignores this Council.
Pakistan reiterated its commitment to working with Gulf countries and international partners to promote de-escalation, maritime security and lasting regional peace and stability.

stories.title: Labourer dies during underpass construction in KP
summary: The rescue authorities received a call that two labourers were trapped under the soil, according to a statement issued by the rescue service.
It said two ambulances were dispatched to the site soon after receiving the call, adding that the teams immediately began relief operations and safely recovered one trapped labourer alive.
However, the search continued, and the rescue personnel later recovered the body of a 28-year-old labourer, Naveed.

stories.title: Two suspects held for murdering minor boy in KP's Lakki
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Police arrested two suspects during a raid on Friday in connection with the murder of a two-year-old boy.

Speaking at a press conference here, District Police Officer (DPO) Sajjad Ahmad Sahibzada said that on Oct 28, Sifatullah, 27, reported to police that his son Sohail, 2, had gone missing while playing outside his house in the Wanda Shahabkhel area.

He said that there was some writing on the corpse, and all these elements helped track down the suspect. “The suspect’s home is located at a stone’s throw from the victim’s house, and that human intelligence was utilised to locate him,” he added.

stories.title: Policeman booked for allegedly aiding woman prisoner to escape in Islamabad
summary: The next day a three-members’ police team – a lady ASI, a lady constable and a constable/police driver - took the beggars, including the woman, to the court of assistant commissioner sub-divisional magistrate city for the hearing.
The court’s order and the beggars were handed over to the police driver, and the lady ASI left from the spot for the hearing of another case.

Investigations over the matter, including footages of the CCTVs installed there, revealed that the police driver, allegedly in collusion with the family of the woman, helped her escape from the parking of the district courts.

stories.title: Minor boy’s body recovered from Karachi's Lyari river
summary: Edhi volunteers launched a search operation and later found his body floating in the river near Gulbahar.
Two die in hit-and-run accident Two people were killed when an unidentified vehicle hit their motorcycle on the Superhighway.
In the second incident, a motorcyclist, identified as Qasim Khan, 65, was killed when an unidentified vehicle hit him near the Sunday Bazaar in Ayub Goth, New Karachi.

stories.title: ‘Country’s first sponge park’ to save rainwater, cut urban flooding risk in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: A water sensitive sponge park, which was recently inaugurated in Gulberg Town, will help manage rainwater as it has the capacity to hold up to 100,000 gallons during the monsoon events, experts associated with World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-P) said on Friday.

The WWF-P in collaboration with the Gulberg Town Municipal Corporation and GSK (GlaxoSmithKline) has introduced a unique urban green space design at Jamali Park in Federal B Area, Block 8, to manage rainwater, enhance infiltration and reduce surface run-off.

It was officially inaugurated as Pakistan’s first water sensitive sponge park at a ceremony that brought together representatives from government, academia, civil society members, corporate partners and local residents.

stories.title: Balochistan Liberation Front terrorist jailed for 48 years in Chinese engineers’ attack case
summary: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court has sentenced a terrorist belonging to the banned Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) to a total of 48 years in prison for carrying out an attack on a car carrying two Chinese engineers near Gulbai Bridge in 2021.
He added that during the initial interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed his crime that in 2021, he along with co-accused Nasir Baloch had attacked the Chinese engineers.
The court noted that the attack on Chinese nationals, in the circumstances established in the present case, could not be treated merely as an ordinary offence of attempted murder.

stories.title: Rs2.5m recovered from ‘fake’ faith healer in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Friday claimed to have recovered Rs2.5 million from a woman posing as a faith healer, who allegedly defrauded women online by offering spiritual treatment for their problems.
The NCCIA said a woman fell victim to financial fraud through a Facebook page titled “Qurani Wazaif,” operated by a woman posing as a peerni.
She later realised that she had been defrauded and approached the agency.= Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

stories.title: Conductor punished for pushing woman off bus in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A private transport company had to sack a conductor who pushed a woman off a bus when she was trying to board the vehicle at a terminal here on Friday, after a video of the episode went viral, grabbing the attention of the Punjab government.

Some passersby recorded video of the incident and shared it on social media, triggering public outrage and the government’s reaction.The video shows the woman was trying to board the bus when the conductor pushed her.
Taking notice of the incident, Punjab Minister for Transport and Mass Transit Bilal Akbar Khan said the conductor had been sacked by the transport company.

stories.title: Police get remand of PTI leader Mian Usman Akram in May 9 case
summary: The investigating officer asked the court to allow shifting of Akram to jail to conduct an identification parade.
Earlier, the Lahore High Court disposed of a petition challenging Akram’s detention after the Punjab government withdrew his detention order.
A law officer informed the court that the notification regarding Akram’s detention had been withdrawn.

stories.title: K-P Governor Kundi suspends provincial gold mining leases amid illegal mining concerns
summary: On Wednesday, at least 11 police personnel, including a deputy superintendent of police (DSP) and a sub-inspector, were martyred and 12 others were injured when terrorists ambushed a police party conducting an operation against an illegal gold mining network in Kohat.

According to a statement issued by the office of the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Peshawar, the Kohat police had launched a major operation against an illegal gold mining network allegedly operating through a nexus between terrorists and criminal elements.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi says 80 per cent of the revenue generated from illegal mining goes to Afghanistan.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly speaker endorses referendum proposal on new provinces
summary: LAHORE: Endorsing a proposal to hold a referendum on the creation of new provinces in the country, Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan says the will of the masses holds supremacy over the opinion of elected representatives on matters of public importance.

Speaking to a private television channel, Rana Sana pointed out that the question of who holds the authority to conduct such a referendum remained unresolved, adding that any constitutional process regarding the carving out of new units would have to go through the parliament.
During his media talk in Lahore, Speaker Khan also touched upon broader political and governance issues.
